summary: Round r1 (restricted network). No values retrieved; all empirical items pending. Benchmark labour indicators come from NLFS 2017/18 (19th ICLS concept), with NLSS IV 2022/23 as a non-LFS intermediate point and NLFS 2024/25 (fieldwork confirmed by an NSO/ILO ToR and 2026 news; report not located) as the future base; ILOSTAT harmonised and modelled series are cross-checks only (C-07). Output per worker by sector is defined as NSO GVA by industry over survey employment by industry on the same FY and NA vintage. Social-protection coverage is split into non-contributory allowances (DoNIDCR/MoF), the contributory SSF, public-service pensions, ILO SDG 1.3.1 and NLSS IV household receipt. Seventeen leads: four search-verified, nine shared, four general-knowledge URLs marked unverified.

findings.claim: Q1: Labour force participation rate, employment-to-population ratio and unemployment rate (15+), by sex, from NLFS 2017/18.
Q1: Composite labour underutilisation (LU4) and time-related underemployment, NLFS 2017/18.
Q1: Informal employment rate (share of employed in informal employment, incl. agriculture and excluding agriculture) and informal-sector employment share, NLFS 2017/18.
findings.note: Keep NSO national definition and ILOSTAT harmonised SDG 8.3.1 as separate observations.

findings.claim: Q1: Participation and unemployment from NLSS IV 2022/23.
findings.note: NLSS IV is a living-standards survey, not an LFS; reference period and question sequence differ; not directly comparable to NLFS - record as separate series.
Survey reported as under way/recent (10B-L04, 10B-L05); report not located. Will supersede 2017/18 as base.

findings.claim: Q1: ILO modelled estimates (ILOEST) of LFPR and unemployment for years without surveys.
findings.note: Model estimates, calendar-year; used only to fill gaps as labelled estimates, never as survey facts (C-07).

findings.claim: Q2: Output per worker by sector (agriculture; industry incl. manufacturing, construction; services sub-sectors) = NSO GVA by industry / NLFS employment by industry, FY2017/18.
findings.note: Numerator: NA GVA at constant and current prices for FY2017/18 (vintage matters after rebasing); denominator: NLFS 2017/18 employment by NSIC section. Both FY.

findings.claim: Q2: Output per worker by sector for FY2022/23 using NLSS IV employment and for FY2024/25 using NLFS 2024/25 when released.
findings.note: Denominator concept differs by survey; report both and flag break.

findings.claim: Q2: Aggregate output per worker (SDG 8.2.1) from ILOSTAT, constant 2021 PPP international dollars.
findings.note: Cross-check; calendar-year, modelled employment. Unit code for PPP dollars not in units.py - store as index or request unit addition (see challenge to 01C).

findings.claim: Q3: Contributory social-security coverage - SSF contributors and employers; share of employees with employer pension/social-security contributions (NLFS).
findings.note: SSF administrative data (10B-L12) and NLFS 2017/18 employee benefit tables.

findings.claim: Q3: Non-contributory social security allowance beneficiaries by category and total outlay.
Q3: SDG 1.3.1 population covered by at least one social-protection benefit, and by function.
findings.note: ILO WSPDB (10B-L14, 10B-L15); calendar reference year per indicator.

findings.claim: Q3: Share of households receiving any social transfer (NLSS IV).

NLFS rounds are the benchmark for labour indicators. NLFS 2017/18 applies the 19th ICLS work concept (own-use production excluded from employment); NLFS 2008 is not comparable without re-tabulation. This is to be confirmed from the 2017/18 methodology chapter (10B-L02).
Output per worker is computed only with numerator and denominator on the same FY and the same NA vintage; no splicing across NA rebasings without a documented back-cast (from 01A).
Workers abroad are excluded from domestic employment denominators (they are outside the NLFS resident frame); remittance income is not treated as domestic output.

data_gaps: NLFS 2024/25 report and release date not located.
No LFS between FY2017/18 and FY2024/25; NLSS IV labour module differs in design, so trend comparisons carry a concept break.
NA GVA vintage for FY2017/18 after the latest rebasing not confirmed (depends on 01A).
SSF and DoNIDCR administrative series not located as downloadable tables (landing pages only, unverified).
Wages: no regular official wage series by sector located; NLFS earnings tables only.
Informality by province and sector cross-tab for FY2022/23 onward requires NLSS IV microdata access.

assumptions.text: NLFS is the benchmark for labour indicators; NLSS IV and ILO modelled series are separate observations and are not spliced with NLFS.
Sectoral output per worker uses identical FY and NA vintage for numerator and denominator; industry mapping documented.
Migrant workers abroad are outside domestic employment; they are handled by 23A/10C as a separate stock.
Labour-input paths beyond survey years (participation, unemployment) are labelled assumptions for 01A, varied in sensitivity analysis.

challenges.text: Labour input for growth accounting should use NLFS employment (19th ICLS) with 10C resident working-age paths, not WPP working-age totals; PWT emp is a cross-check only.
C-07 accepted; add a concept-break flag between NLFS 2017/18, NLSS IV 2022/23 and NLFS 2024/25.
units.py has no code for PPP international dollars; ILO SDG 8.2.1 output per worker cannot be stored in its native unit. Request a unit addition via Agent 00 rather than mislabelling.
Accepted: NLSS IV provincial receipt shares with standard errors; 10B will use the same NLSS IV observation set for social-transfer receipt to avoid double ingestion.

uncertainty: High for r1. Main uncertainties: (i) the concept break between NLFS 2017/18, NLSS IV and NLFS 2024/25 may exceed true change in unemployment/participation; (ii) informality measurement depends on the definition (NSO national vs ILO harmonised); (iii) sectoral productivity is sensitive to NA vintage and to the classification of own-account agricultural workers; (iv) social-protection coverage mixes administrative counts (possible duplicates across schemes) and survey receipt. Four lead URLs are general knowledge and unverified.
